steps.text: DeskPort shares one computer and lets your other devices use its desktop.
The computer being used is the host; the device you sit at is the client. A computer can be both.
Devices are bound to each other once. Access is approved on the host and can be withdrawn there.
Open Sharing in the top bar and choose Start sharing.
Grant screen recording and accessibility access when asked. Sharing runs without them, but the picture or input will not work.
A dot under the sharing icon means this computer is currently shared.
Devices on the same network appear on the device list by themselves.
Use Add device on the add card for a computer on another network, and enter its address.
Selecting a device the first time asks the host for access; approve the request there.
If another device is already connected, you are asked whether to take over. Taking over disconnects that device.
Edit in the top bar starts edit mode; drag cards to reorder them.
Drop one device onto another to group them, like folders on a phone home screen.
Set alias in the card's menu renames a device for this device only.
Refresh checks saved devices again and looks for new ones.
On a computer, Full screen in the device's settings decides how a connection to that device opens.
On a computer, Ctrl+Alt+Shift+X switches full screen on and off during a connection; on a phone or tablet it brings back the floating button.
Phones and tablets always show the remote desktop on the whole screen. Tap the floating button for the keyboard; hold it for the menu.
The host can ask a connected device to leave full screen; it never forces it into full screen.
The remote desktop follows your window size, so resizing the window resizes the remote desktop.
Virtual screen decides what happens to the host's own screens while you are connected.
Desktop fine tuning makes everything on the remote desktop larger or smaller.
These settings are saved per device.
A device shown as offline is usually asleep, on another network, or not sharing.
Refresh in the top bar re-checks every saved device.
Report a problem in Settings collects a log archive you can attach to an issue. Review it before sharing it.
